headline: Survey points to a 7% jump in US scrap for November
detail: Fastmarkets' monthly survey came in at 70.6, which implies about a 7.1% rise, and mill bids are running $20–$30 a gross ton higher. Chicago's settle should firm up within days.

headline: China buyers scramble for copper as premiums hit new highs
detail: South China spot premiums rose another 200 yuan to about 1,950 yuan a ton, and the Yangshan import premium reached $205, a 12-year high. Tight physical supply is what is holding copper up.

headline: Democrats' win leaves metal tariffs in Trump's hands
detail: Steel, aluminum and copper duties stay under presidential authority despite the new Congress, and BMO flags possible refined-copper tariffs from January. The Senate has a procedural vote on mine permitting set for Nov 9.

headline: Gold settles up 3.3% after the Democratic sweep
detail: Gold closed near $4,059 and silver near $52.10 Wednesday as the dollar and yields fell. Friday's jobs report and the Fed's December meeting are the next tests.

headline: Palladium jumps about 7.5% and platinum nearly 6%
detail: Palladium climbed back near $1,000 from a 16-month low and platinum reached about $1,500 on the weaker dollar. If it holds, converter values should improve.

headline: Copper shrugs off the election and holds near $14,000
detail: LME three-month copper closed at $14,015 Wednesday, down 0.14%, then edged up early Thursday. A divided Washington and cheaper oil helped, while worries about AI spending capped gains.

headline: Clean copper scrap recovers 2 cents after a 16-cent drop
detail: ScrapMonster's North American report had the clean copper grades up 2 cents a pound for Nov 4, following Tuesday's slide. Steel and stainless grades held flat.

headline: Nucor lifts hot-rolled again to $1,280, a 15th straight rise
detail: Lead times stand at three to five weeks. Steel buyers in a Steel Market Update survey say supply, not price, is now their main worry, which supports mill demand for scrap.

headline: US raw steel output hits its highest since 2008
detail: Weekly production reached the top level since August 2008, led by Southern mills. Strong mill runs mean more scrap buying.

headline: Top new copper mine cuts its 2027 forecast again
detail: Ivanhoe lowered Kamoa-Kakula's 2027 output to 300,000–350,000 tons from 380,000–420,000 and raised its cost outlook. Less mine supply adds to the tight copper market.

headline: Dollar near a five-week low, December hike still likely
detail: Markets put about a 79% chance on a Fed hike next month even as the dollar index sits near 101.5. A weaker dollar helps metals; a hike would push the other way.

headline: Oil falls about 8% on hopes for US-Iran talks
detail: WTI ended near $88 and Brent near $95 Wednesday. Cheaper energy cuts metal producers' costs and eases inflation fears.

headline: Nickel leads the metals higher
detail: LME cash nickel rose 1.7% to $15,465 and three-month prices gained more, the best of the base metals Wednesday. Stainless scrap tends to follow nickel.

headline: LME aluminum rebounds to about $3,067 on low China stocks
detail: Three-month aluminum closed up 0.87% Wednesday, with Chinese warehouse stocks at about 521,000 tons. Century Aluminum reports results after today's close.

headline: Sherritt furloughs nearly half its Canadian staff
detail: About 280 workers are out for an expected 90 days as US sanctions on Cuba cut feed to its Alberta nickel refinery. It trims a small part of nickel supply in a market that is still oversupplied.

headline: Iron ore climbs 1% to about $92
detail: Prices reached their highest in about a month even as China's own steel market stays soft. Higher ore costs help scrap compete as a mill input.

headline: US auto sales pace slips to 15.6 million
detail: October sales were about 1.3 million, up 4% from a year ago, but the annual pace was the first below 16 million since February. Slower sales mean less steel, aluminum and eventually fewer end-of-life flows.

headline: Construction spending fell 1.9% in September
detail: The drop far missed forecasts, with residential spending down 5.5% while nonresidential rose 1.1%. Weak housing cuts demand for copper wire and pipe.

headline: Data centers carry nonresidential building
detail: Data center spending rose 8.6% in September and is up about 90% from a year ago. These projects use a lot of copper, aluminum and steel.

headline: China's factories slip back into contraction
detail: The official October index fell to 49.3 from 50.1, its lowest since July, with export orders at 48.7. Softer factory demand is the main drag on base metals.

headline: China services growth slows to 50.8
detail: The private October survey fell from 51.6 as price cuts met rising costs. It adds to signs of a cooling economy.

headline: Lutnick restarts Canada talks on metal tariffs
detail: Sources say the Commerce Secretary reopened talks about 10 days ago, focused on duties of up to 50% on steel, aluminum and copper. A deal could cut the US aluminum premium and scrap values with it.

headline: Private hiring beats forecasts, service prices stay hot
detail: ADP showed 86,000 new jobs against 69,000 expected, and the ISM services index was 54.5 with its prices gauge at 73. Firm data keeps a December hike in play.

headline: Highland Valley copper strike passes a week
detail: About 1,200 USW workers walked out Oct 24 at Canada's biggest copper mine and no bargaining dates are set. A long strike would tighten concentrate supply further.

headline: Zinc holds near a one-month high on smelter trouble
detail: Problems at Korea Zinc, Kazzinc and YoungPoong, plus weak Chinese ore imports, pushed treatment fees to record lows. That keeps zinc and die-cast scrap supported.

headline: US steel scrap grades rose $10–$15 a ton Tuesday
detail: ScrapMonster's report had heavy melt, shredded and structural up $15 a metric ton and sheet up $10. The move comes ahead of the November settle.

headline: Turkish scrap keeps rising
detail: Kallanish says import prices extended last week's rebound as suppliers lifted their targets. Firmer export demand helps support US scrap.

headline: Gold pushes on to about $4,120 overnight
detail: Kitco quoted gold up another $60 and silver near $52.40 early Thursday. Friday's payrolls are the next catalyst.

headline: Mixed supply picture behind the PGM bounce
detail: The WPIC expects a 265,000-ounce platinum surplus this year, while a Nornickel furnace overhaul could run into 2028. That leaves the rebound leaning on the dollar more than on tight supply.

headline: Ford lifts its 2026 metal cost estimate to about $2.5 billion
detail: The increase from about $2 billion cites copper and steel, among other costs. Automakers may push suppliers harder as a result.
